CA.name: American bistort
CA.citation: Calscape; native range confirmed from Alaska and British Columbia south into California and east into the Rockies. Also documented as western bistort, smokeweed, snakeweed. Genus/species-specific, distinguished from the European Bistorta officinalis, which shares the name's etymology (Latin bis- + torta, 'twice-twisted') but is a distinct Eurasian species

US.name: American bistort
US.citation: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center; Idaho Fish and Game Species Catalog. Roots historically used in soups/stews by the Blackfoot and Cherokee, and as a poultice by the Miwok
